content.comment_body: I'm facing difficulties connecting my PC to [product_name] V7. Despite searching extensively, communication seems impossible. Is there a specific communication cable that works? My cable is a [company_name] programming USB cable, article number [article_no]. Any suggestions?
Have you installed the required USB drivers?
I've installed all the drivers, but I still get an error with a question mark showing up for the USB port. Could someone help me identify what might be causing this?
Hello [user_name], why do you see a question mark on the USB port? Is your cable RS232, possibly using an adapter? For reference, see [url].
Could you share a screenshot of the error message?

I purchased this adapter from Amazon Germany for about 12 €. It works perfectly on my new computer running Windows 7. The driver software comes included, and you will see a virtual COM port, which you need to select in the [product_name] software. It also works reliably on my old Windows XP machine. Digitus DA-70156 USB Serial Adapter USB 2.0

I wanted to thank you for the information. It's important to note that not all USB to RS232 converters are compatible with [company_name] devices, especially on 64-bit Windows or Windows 7. Perhaps we should create a thread listing converters that do work. Also, replacing hardware like these can sometimes cause driver conflicts. I recommend uninstalling associated software and only using one brand of converter per PC.

Check your PC using Microsoft Management Console (mmc.exe) under PORTs (USB/COM/LPT), and remove any device with a question mark. If you connect the USB [article_no] [company_name] [product_name] PC cable, look for Silicon Labs CP210x USB to UART Bridge (COM9). PS: Original installation files are named CP210x_VCP_Win2K_XP_S2K3_Vista.exe (6MB) in the CD's WINDOWS directory.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter persistent issues connecting their PCs to [product_name] using a [company_name] USB programming cable. Common problems involve USB driver installation failures, hardware compatibility between USB-to-RS232 adapters and [company_name] devices, and difficulty getting drivers to work across different versions of Windows. Compatibility varies greatly with adapters and drivers, especially on newer operating systems, and users sometimes face device driver conflicts and must pay attention to proper device management.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate straightforward communication between their PC and [product_name] with easy and reliable driver installation, and expect connections to work without hardware compatibility concerns.
